facts.text: Lowry Field was named after Second Lieutenant Francis Lowry, the only Colorado pilot killed in World War I.
The original Lowry airfield sat on land seized by the Colorado National Guard, bordered by East 38th Avenue between Dahlia and Holly.
Lowry’s motto, Sustineo Alas—'I Sustain the Wings'—is emblazoned on many historic buildings still standing today.
On August 31, 1927, Charles Lindbergh landed at Lowry Field for a publicity tour after his famous trans‑Atlantic flight.
After the base closed, many original hangars, offices, and housing were creatively repurposed into homes, offices, and cultural spaces.
Lowry Air Force Base served as a U.S. Army Air Forces training site during WWII and later as a U.S. Air Force training center during the Cold War.
